s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disease with autoimmune features, characterized by skin, joint, and lung involvement, with a prolonged course of symptoms and significant weight loss
salient_findings: Symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints with ulcers
Dyspigmentation and atrophy of distal fingers
Bibasilar rales on auscultation
Elevated ferritin levels
Lymphocytopenia with positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies
Restrictive lung disease with decreased diffusing capacity
key_facts: 7-month history of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, arthralgias, hand swelling, tender ulcerations, hair loss, and weight loss
Previous hospitalization for hypoxia
Prior treatment with prednisone
Symmetric joint swelling preventing fist formation
Normal capillaroscopy
Ulcerated lichenoid papules on palmar IP creases
Oxford Scale muscle strength 5 of 5 throughout
Elevated ferritin levels (1543 ng/mL)
Lymphocytopenia with CD3: 328 μL, CD4: 233 μL, CD8: 85 μL
Positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies
Positive immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies (19.5 units)
Normal prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, tissue thromboplastin
Chest CT showing hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial thickening, and perilymphatic ground glass opacities
Pulmonary function tests showing restrictive disease with decreased diffusing capacity (33% predicted)
Skin biopsy showing orthokeratosis, minimal basal vacuolar change, pigment incontinence, and diffuse vasculopathy with fibrin thrombi

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies, lymphocytopenia, and elevated ferritin levels

shortlist.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies and interstitial lung disease

shortlist.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of systemic lupus erythematosus, scleroderma, and polymyositis features

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsy showing orthokeratosis, minimal basal vacuolar change, and pigment incontinence

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial lung disease, and elevated ferritin levels

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial lung disease, and skin lesions, along with elevated ferritin levels and lymphocytopenia, are more consistent with sarcoidosis. The presence of non-caseating granulomas is not explicitly mentioned, but the overall clinical picture and the absence of specific autoantibodies point towards sarcoidosis.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient lacks specific autoantibodies such as anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm, and the clinical presentation does not fully align with SLE.

rejected.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not primarily involve the exocrine glands, and the presence of anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies is not sufficient to diagnose Sjögren's Syndrome in this context.

rejected.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: The patient's clinical features do not meet the criteria for MCTD, which typically includes a combination of features from SLE, scleroderma, and polymyositis/dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: The patient's muscle strength is normal (Oxford Scale 5 of 5), and the skin biopsy does not show the characteristic changes of dermatomyositis, such as perifascicular atrophy.
